Just Move: Clean City Messy Battle is a small, straightforward top-down action game that aims for quick, accessible fun rather than complexity. Developed and published by daminggede, the title enters Early Access with the clear intent to expand, but in its current form it offers a compact experience centered on fast-paced movement, automatic shooting, and a sequence of short missions designed to be played in rapid succession. It doesn’t try to redefine the top-down shooter formula; instead, it presents itself as a light, arcade-like action title built around mobility, positioning, and simple progression systems. Because of this, it is best approached as an early-stage project with room to grow rather than a fully polished or content-rich experience. The core gameplay loop revolves around navigating tight, city-themed arenas while your character automatically fires at enemies whenever they enter your range. This mechanic defines the game’s feel: it eliminates the need to aim manually, shifting the focus entirely to movement. Dodging projectiles, weaving through clusters of enemies, and staying just close enough to engage while not getting overwhelmed form the heart of combat. For players who enjoy the idea of reactive dodging and straightforward action without complex controls, this approach can feel intuitive and immediately approachable. It offers a pick-up-and-play rhythm reminiscent of simple mobile or arcade shooters, which can be appealing in short bursts. Content-wise, the game currently offers ten different map types, each with its own layout and theme—rooftops, gardens, bridges, parking lots, narrow corridors, and other urban settings meant to vary the flow of encounters. While these maps do add some visual variety, the limited number of enemy types and the small pool of available weapons make the actual moment-to-moment gameplay feel uniform. Missions, which number around one hundred in total, tend to rely on variations of the same combat scenarios rather than introducing new objectives or mechanics. As a result, while the game provides quantity, the quality of variation depends heavily on whether you find the core loop satisfying enough to repeat multiple times. Progression comes in the form of experience and currency gained from successful missions. This allows players to unlock or upgrade weapons, characters, or other enhancements aimed at giving a small sense of growth. These systems are currently simple but functional: they give you a mild incentive to keep playing and slowly improve your character’s effectiveness. However, because the weapons themselves behave similarly and the upgrade paths are limited, the sense of progression may not feel meaningful for long. This is an area where the developer’s promise to add more weapons and enemy types could help significantly, turning the upgrade system into a more engaging part of the experience. The Early Access nature of the game is evident not just in its limited variety but also in its rough edges. The basic auto-shoot system works, but because combat depends almost entirely on proximity and movement, encounters sometimes feel flat or overly predictable. There is little reactive depth—enemies rarely force tactical adjustments beyond staying mobile. Visual and audio feedback is fairly minimal, which further reduces the dynamism of encounters. With only a handful of weapons, limited environmental interactivity, and a small enemy roster, the game currently resembles an early prototype of a potentially more substantial action title. Whether it evolves meaningfully depends on how fully the developer commits to expanding the systems already in place. Another challenge is the lack of community presence or broader player feedback. With only a few visible reviews—and at least one negative—the game has not yet found a sizeable audience. This makes it difficult for new players to gauge what to expect, and for the developer to gather consistent feedback to refine mechanics or balance. The small player base also reinforces the sense that the game is still in a foundational stage, awaiting more content, polish, and visibility before it can establish itself as a minor but enjoyable indie shooter. Despite its current limitations, Just Move: Clean City Messy Battle has the seed of an appealing concept. Its simplicity makes it easy to jump into, its maps provide a bit of visual change, and its mission-based structure gives it clear goals that can be tackled in quick sessions. For players who enjoy minimalist arcade shooters, or who want something lightweight to play on low-end hardware, it may offer a brief but serviceable diversion. The potential for improvements—more weapons, more enemy types, enhanced effects, better map designs—suggests room for growth if the developer remains committed to updating it. In its present state, the game is best understood as a work in progress: a rough, barebones top-down shooter with a functional core, limited depth, and a clear need for expansion. It is not yet a fully satisfying or richly layered experience, but it contains the foundation of one. Those who enjoy early access experimentation or ultra-casual shooters may find it mildly engaging. Others should wait to see how the game evolves, as future updates will ultimately determine whether Just Move: Clean City Messy Battle grows into a polished, replayable action title or remains a short-lived curiosity. Rating: 5/10

俯视角双摇杆射击小游戏，一共 100 关，作为免费喜加一作品，只能说勉强能尝个咸淡，不适合认真游玩。 前 50 关难度极低，只要保持距离用远程武器放风筝就能轻松过关，几乎没有压力。但从 50 关之后难度突然飙升，全图狙击、高伤近战、大范围迫击炮轮番来袭，就算把装备拉满也很难扛住，纯靠数值碾压，毫无策略可言。 武器平衡做得很差，一共 5 把武器，只有初始枪械实用，其余武器伤害高但攻速慢，也没有穿墙、增距等特殊效果，完全没必要换。关卡设计重复、敌人单纯堆属性，玩久了非常枯燥。 整体就是一款体量单薄、难度曲线崩坏的免费小品，适合领来凑成就，不推荐特意花时间玩。

[h3] As a beginner gamedev, I'd be ashamed to release this. [/h3] First of all, it looks and plays like a poorly ported mobile game. Seriously, the only thing they've done is set character movement to WASD. Want to pause the game? Too bad, you can only dream of pressing ESC. Skip past repetetive unlock screens with space? What, are you stupid? You [b]have to[/b] manually click the center of the screen with your mouse after every single level. The gameplay itself is the definition of boring and unbalanced. Image Vampire Survivors, but strip away items, progressive waves of enemies, deep evolution system or just anything cool in general. Devs even dare to put "roguelike", "rougelite", "soulslike" and bunch of other nonsense into the tags, which is just blatant misinformation and misleading the potential customer. And I haven't even mentioned idiotic balance and level design which is hard to even call a "design" in a first place, as it looks like randomly placed assets. There's a world in a game when 1/5th of the map is blocked by cars and enemies do spawn there - enemies, which have the ability to shoot through the cars (you can't) and [b]walk out of your range anytime they want.[/b] Getting all achievements is hell on Earth, as later levels are just throwing tons of unbalanced and miserable enemies at your face the moment you spawn. Even funnier, it doesn't even matter, as currently achievements and this game in general are not visible on your profile - and probably they'll never will be, hopefully. If this game is 95% or even 100% off as you're reading this - trust me, just skip this one. There's no potential here, nothing interesting to find and personally I don't think the developer deserves any money from this at all. If only I could see a single bit of passion poured into this game, then maybe - but I did look around and found nothing.

完全不推荐游玩。 之前免费入库的游戏，试玩了一下，感觉是万万全全的新人练手作品（AI生成可能性微存？） 整体素材就是那种免费的手机游戏通用素材。 七章之前有让人想睡；七章之后堆一大堆黄金狙击手强行提升难度，也没能让人觉得有趣。 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ 游戏内容仅为移动人物进行移动，人物自动索敌并自动射击。 整体一共五把武器，其中四把武器需要在关卡中收集碎片来获得。 一共为：初始机枪，吉他机枪，霰弹枪，一把射击有溅射效果的枪，一把有电流弹射效果的枪。 但是不用担心，除了一二武器（机枪跟吉他机枪）其余都是无用之物。 由于机枪的伤害频率，即使刮痧也能在短时间内输出可用的伤害； 霰弹枪一次性射出三发子弹，但是散射距离太大，除非贴脸，否则很难打出伤害，而且射速慢。 溅射枪一次射出一发溅射炮弹，炮弹爆炸后周围的敌人能受到伤害；但是溅射伤害不高， 且溅射范围也小的可怜，加上射速问题，还是没什么用。 电流弹射枪倒是射速合格，射出去的电流炮弹会弹射到多个敌人上，且范围很远； 但问题是，枪本身的输出极为低下；弹射出去的电流伤害更是可悲；而且由于游戏设定， 受到伤害的敌人也会立刻行动，于是乎使用这把枪基本上就等同于开了群嘲转职成为火车王。 为什么我要一直强调射速呢？ 因为七章之后有个神奇的敌人叫做黄金狙击手；它的特征就是会携带一把黄金狙击枪； 射击基本上是开局无视距离的向玩家方向瞄准，射击子弹碰撞障碍物会进行弹射。 射击一轮三颗子弹后会以光速跑路到另一个方向逃走，随后瞄准进行下一轮射击。 跑路速度会让玩家的自动瞄准望尘莫及，一跑起来就能看见它在前面跑，玩家的子弹在后面追。 只有他停下的时候才是输出的时机，但HP量奇厚无比；基本上要射击好一段时间才能击杀。 加上后期这位是成群结队出现，也就是说开场你就能看见满屏幕的瞄准线， 且每发子弹的伤害很是不低且是三连射且能折射，经常能看到子弹从不知道哪里折射过来。 另外七章会出现一些狙击手存在于完全封闭的环境内，玩家无法进入，但是敌人的子弹可以射出。 这种情况需要先清理周围的敌人，回过头来在敌人的射击缝停止攻击的时候将你自己的子弹灌进去。 很多时候需要不停的调整角度才能让人物射击这些敌人，可以说是作者的恶意了。 另外，游戏的战力感觉并不影响整体伤害，经过使用同一武器，但更换不同战力的人物在同一关卡射击敌人查看伤害的情况下，射击出的伤害完全一致，也就是说人物升级怕是真的只能搏角色一笑了。 而且根据英文评测，此游戏的100个成就完全不会被计入Steam成就总数当中，无法被计入个人资料成就计数。加上七章后的各种恶意，即使是为了成就也不建议游玩这款游戏。 另外根据评测内的“赤石英雄”们的看法，11章以后明显的存在没有做完的痕迹，所有看到这篇评测的人们，速速退怯，莫要入此粪坑。
